- **Writing [templates/harness/LEDGER.md](../templates/harness/LEDGER.md)'s own row for the commit it belongs to, then running `git commit --amend --no-edit` to fold the row into that same commit (per the ledger's "in the same commit" rule), changes the commit's hash — which makes the row's own citation stale again. Amending a second time to fix the citation changes the hash a second time, and so on: the row is content inside the very object whose identity it names, so no amend can ever make it correct.** [story](gotcha-2026-09-17-a-ledger-row-citing-its-own-commit-cannot-converge-by-amen.md)
